title: Refinement invariance of face-cocone evaluations
statement: Use simplicial categories of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting] and the subset-poset simplex model of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. Let $V$ be a finite nonempty linearly ordered set, and let $\mathcal F$ be a family of nonempty subsets of $V$ containing every singleton and closed under taking nonempty subsets. For $F\in\mathcal F$, write $\Delta^F$ for the ordered simplex on $F$. Let $D$ be a small simplicial category and let $f_F:\mathfrak C[\Delta^F]\to D$ be enriched functors strictly compatible under all inclusions $F\subseteq G$ in $\mathcal F$. Write $d_v=f_{\{v\}}(v)$. For $i<j$ in $V$, let $S=(S_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq S_q)$ be a chain of subsets of $[i,j]$ containing $i,j$, with $q\geq0$. A splitting set $R=\{i=a_0<\cdots<a_r=j\}\subseteq S_0$ is admissible if $T_b=S_q\cap[a_{b-1},a_b]\in\mathcal F$ for every $b$. Define $E_R(S)\in D(d_i,d_j)_q$ as the ordered composite of $f_{T_b}$ applied to the restricted flags $(S_t\cap[a_{b-1},a_b])_{t=0}^q$. If $R\subseteq R'\subseteq S_0$ contains the endpoints and $R$ is admissible, then $R'$ is admissible and $E_{R'}(S)=E_R(S)$. Consequently any two admissible splitting sets give the same value; in particular this value equals the value for the canonical splitting set $S_0$.

proof.text: First check the types of the evaluations. If $R=\{a_0<\cdots<a_r\}$ is admissible, every $a_b$ belongs to every $S_t$, since $R\subseteq S_0\subseteq S_t$. For $T_b=S_q\cap[a_{b-1},a_b]$, the restricted flag $X_b=(S_t\cap[a_{b-1},a_b])_{t=0}^q$ therefore consists of subsets of $T_b$ containing its two endpoints, and defines a $q$-simplex of $\mathfrak C[\Delta^{T_b}](a_{b-1},a_b)$ by [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. The inclusions $\{a_b\}\subseteq T_b$ and strict compatibility of the given functors identify their endpoint objects with $d_{a_b}$. Hence their images are composable in degree $q$ in $D$, whose associative simplicial composition is part of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]; the ordered composite defining $E_R(S)$ is well typed.

source.place: Definitions 1.1.5.1 and 1.1.5.3, printed pp.20–22; agent expansion of the face-cocone calculation underlying the proof of Theorem 2.2.5.1, printed p.90.

proof.text: Check admissibility under a refinement $R\subseteq R'\subseteq S_0$. Consecutive elements $u<v$ of $R'$ lie in one old interval $[a_{b-1},a_b]$: an old splitting vertex strictly between them would also belong to $R'$, contradicting consecutiveness. Their new support is $S_q\cap[u,v]\subseteq T_b$. It is nonempty, since $u,v\in S_0\subseteq S_q$. The closure hypothesis on $\mathcal F$ therefore puts it in $\mathcal F$. This proves admissibility of $R'$, including when some new interval has no interior vertices.

source.place: Definitions 1.1.5.1 and 1.1.5.3, printed pp.20–22; agent expansion of the face-cocone calculation underlying the proof of Theorem 2.2.5.1, printed p.90.

proof.text: For one insertion, take $c\in S_0\setminus R$ and the unique consecutive $a<b$ of $R$ with $a<c<b$. Set $T=S_q\cap[a,b]$, $T^-=S_q\cap[a,c]$, $T^+=S_q\cap[c,b]$, and write $X,X^-,X^+$ for the corresponding restricted flags. They are valid mapping simplices, since $a,c,b\in S_0$, and $T^-,T^+\in\mathcal F$ by Step 2. Inside $\mathfrak C[\Delta^T]$, composition in [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching] gives $X=X^+\circ X^-$: in each degree entry, $(S_t\cap[a,c])\cup(S_t\cap[c,b])=S_t\cap[a,b]$, and a flag in a poset nerve is determined by its entries. Here the two factors are viewed under the face inclusions. Apply the composition-preserving axiom of the enriched functor $f_T$ and its strict compatibility with these inclusions to obtain $f_T(X)=f_{T^+}(X^+)\circ f_{T^-}(X^-)$. Thus the old factor at $[a,b]$ is replaced by exactly the two new factors; all other factors are unchanged. Associativity of composition in $D$ from [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting] gives $E_{R\cup\{c\}}(S)=E_R(S)$. This uses only union composition and the defining functor axiom, not a separate comparison theorem.

source.place: Definitions 1.1.5.1 and 1.1.5.3, printed pp.20–22; agent expansion of the face-cocone calculation underlying the proof of Theorem 2.2.5.1, printed p.90.

proof.text: Induct on the finite number $|R'\setminus R|$ to prove equality for every refinement. If this number is zero, $R'=R$ and the evaluations are identical. Otherwise choose $c\in R'\setminus R$. Step 2 makes $R\cup\{c\}$ admissible, Step 3 gives $E_{R\cup\{c\}}(S)=E_R(S)$, and the induction hypothesis applies to $R\cup\{c\}\subseteq R'$ with one fewer missing vertex. It gives $E_{R'}(S)=E_{R\cup\{c\}}(S)$, hence the required equality.

source.place: Definitions 1.1.5.1 and 1.1.5.3, printed pp.20–22; agent expansion of the face-cocone calculation underlying the proof of Theorem 2.2.5.1, printed p.90.

proof.text: For any admissible $R$, the refinement $R\subseteq S_0$ and Steps 2 and 4 show that $S_0$ is admissible and $E_R(S)=E_{S_0}(S)$. Consequently two admissible splitting sets $R_1,R_2$ have equal evaluations by comparison with this same $E_{S_0}(S)$, even if neither contains the other. This consequence is conditional on the existence of an admissible splitting; the hypotheses do not assert that one always exists.
